findings.issue: Five external calls lose their function and arguments (positions(bytes32) in mint; onERC721Received(address,address,uint256,bytes) in both safeTransferFrom; transfer(caller, amount1Owed) and transferFrom(payer, caller, amount1Owed) on token1 in the callback), two require messages ('ST', 'STF') stay raw memory reverts, and the Collect event's data stays a memory range. The same constructs are decoded well where the memory base is a constant (token0's payments in the same callback, positions() in increaseLiquidity). Cause: memory addressed from an unknown free-memory pointer is not resolved. mem[64] becomes a phi after an if/else that allocates in one branch (EnumerableMap._set's push of a MapEntry, the branches of pay(), isContract's branches) and then (a) mem[64] is not folded even right after 'mem[64] = mem[64] + 58' (1863 -> 1870), and (b) words written at _72 + 36 and _72 + 68 are not read back through the copy of mem[_72 + 32 len 68]; mem[_72] = 68 written at 1225 is re-read as unknown at 1229.
findings.rule: Memory offsets used by an execution that gets past the access are below 2^64 (expanding memory that far costs more gas than any client allows), and so are calldata.size and return_data.size; hence 'b + c' never wraps for an SSA base b and a small constant c. Ranges at b + c1 and b + c2 are then disjoint by their constants alone, and a range at b + c is disjoint from [0, 96) when a range analysis bounds b (every store to mem[64] is a constant >= 96 or the old value plus a non-wrapping amount; a phi keeps the minimum). With that: fold mem[64] to its last stored value, resolve reads of a buffer built at b + k, and decode selector + arguments of the call / data of the log as the text already does for constant bases.
findings.verified: reading only (bytecode semantics are right: text_check passes on this contract; the call buffers were traced by hand against the source's abi.encodeWithSelector)

findings.issue: 12 of the text's 15 while loops are memory-to-memory copies of a bytes/string, not loops of the source; only 3 whiles are real loops (multicall's for, the zero-initialisation of new bytes[](n), the return encoding's outer loop). Calldata/returndata/storage copies are shown as copy lines, memory-to-memory ones never are.
findings.rule: Shape A 's = 0; while s < n: mem[d + s] = mem[a + s]; s = s + 32' then 'if s > n: mem[d + n] = 0' is exactly 'mem[d len n] = mem[a len n]' then 'if n % 32: mem[d + n len 32] = 0'. Shape B 'while k >= 32: mem[t] = mem[s]; s, t += 32; k -= 32' followed by the masked merge of the last partial word is exactly 'mem[d len n] = mem[a len n]'. Both hold for word-wise forward copies when d <= a or the ranges are disjoint (provable here with the base + constant reasoning of the first finding). Also floor32(max(31, n)) == floor32(n).

findings.source: FullMath.mulDiv (512-bit mul/div with Newton inverse) reached from LiquidityAmounts.getLiquidityForAmount0/1 and the fee updates 'FullMath.mulDiv(feeGrowthInside0LastX128 - position.feeGrowthInside0LastX128, liquidity, Q128)'
findings.issue: Each inlined mulDiv is unreadable: (a - b) * c is distributed into a*c - b*c in every occurrence of prod0, the odd part of the denominator d / (d & -d) is substituted about 20 times per line, two Newton steps are merged into one degree-4 polynomial (_72 = 4*_71 - 6*_71*_71*D + 4*_71^3*D^2 - _71^4*D^3), and -2^96, -2^128, -2^160 are printed in decimal beside the same powers in hex.
findings.rule: Do not distribute * over + / - (or merge consecutive multiplications into a polynomial) when that duplicates a non-atomic operand; bind a non-trivial subexpression used more than twice to a temporary (here d = address(_69 - _68), twos = d & -d, dd = d / twos, prod0 = (rd - f) * L, mm = mulmod(rd - f, L, -1)). Print a negated power of two like the positive one (-0x1000000000000000000000000, or -(x << 96)), and a - b rather than -b + a.

notes: All 39 ABI functions and the fallback/receive reviewed against the source; no semantic error found. mint's TickMath / getLiquidityForAmounts part (text 1521-1803) is the same expansion as increaseLiquidity's and was reviewed by structure. Checked by disassembly: (1) TickMath's 'type(uint256).max / ratio' has a div-by-zero INVALID in the bytecode (pc 16548-16559) that the text omits ('_36 = -1 / _34'); it is unreachable (ratio >= ~2^52 by interval arithmetic over the 19 constants), so the text is exact. (2) 'revert with Error(string reason), 32, 50, ..., mem[mem[64] + 118 len 14]' (821, 1068) is faithful: solc's legacy encoder CODECOPYs the 50-byte literal without zero padding (the string sits in the data section at byte 22507), so the last 14 bytes really are stale memory. Smaller points not filed: baseURI() printed as 'const baseURI = 32, 0' (an empty string); the fallback's 'require calldata.size < 4' is implied by the next 'require not calldata.size'; collect/decrease keep an early 'mem[501] = sha3(...)' and later print 'mem[501]' inside the pool address (first finding's cause). Loop count: 1 explicit loop (multicall) + 35 implicit (dynamic copies, new bytes[], abi encode/decode of strings and bytes[]); copies resolved into fixed words counted as unrolled (callback token0 payments, sweepToken, permit's isValidSignature bytes, pool.mint's bytes data x2). evmrun is not in build-cmp3 (it is in /home/claude/wt-cxx/cxx/build); no execution run for this contract, nothing left to reproduce.
summary: Faithful on every path checked, including rare and owner-only ones, and all loops are present; but memory addressed from an unknown free-memory pointer is never resolved, which hides the function and arguments of 5 external calls, leaves 12 memory copies as while loops and prints about 130 dead memory writes, and the inlined FullMath.mulDiv blocks are unreadable multi-thousand-character polynomials.
